The proposed answer is wrong. The correct area is **200**.

**Setup.** Put the external homothety center H at the origin, with the line of centers along the x-axis. Let θ be the half-angle between the tangents, with c = cos θ and s = sin θ. Then O₁ = (a, 0), O₂ = (b, 0), and the tangency points are U = (ac², ±acs) on Γ₁ and V = (bc², ±bcs) on Γ₂.

**Trapezoid area.** U₁U₂ and V₁V₂ are both perpendicular to the line of centers, so they are parallel. Their lengths are 2acs and 2bcs, and the horizontal distance between them is |b − a|c². So

Area = c³s·|b² − a²|.

**Determining θ and x.** Let P = (x, 5), since PQ = 10 and PQ is perpendicular to the line of centers. The distances from P to the two tangent lines y = ±x·tan θ are |xs − 5c| and |xs + 5c|. Setting these equal to {3, 12} forces xs = 7.5 and c = 0.9, so s = √19/10 and x = 75/√19. (This matches the slope m = √19/9 in the proposed solution.)

**Determining a and b.** Subtracting the two circle equations x² − 2ax + a²c² + 25 = 0 and the analogous one for b gives a + b = 2x/c². Both a and b are roots of c²t² − 2xt + (x² + 25) = 0. The discriminant reduces to x²s² − 25c² = 56.25 − 20.25 = 36, so a, b = (x ± 6)/c². Hence |b − a| = 12/c² and |b + a| = 2x/c², giving |b² − a²| = 24x/c⁴.

**Area.**

Area = c³s · 24x/c⁴ = 24·(xs)/c = 24·7.5/0.9 = 200.

**Numerical check.** With a ≈ 28.648 and b ≈ 13.833, the vertices are U₁(23.205, 11.239), U₂(23.205, −11.239), V₂(11.205, −5.427), V₁(11.205, 5.427). The shoelace formula gives an area of 200, and P = (17.205, 5) lies on both circles with the correct distances 3 and 12 to the tangents.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
